chunk_findings.detail: The new `reuse_parsed = true` assertion is placed outside the loop that exercises the real entry points: the false-direction body uses the loop’s `call()` and `label`, while the added block is dedented and hard-codes `reporting.loops(repo)`. This only proves that `reporting.loops` honors the true knob. If any other real entry point covered by that loop hard-codes `LogConfig(reuse_parsed=False)`, the false-direction assertion still passes because the cache is empty, and the new true-direction assertion still passes because `reporting.loops` populates the cache. Thus the test named for “real entry points” can still pass while a different real entry point ignores `[log] reuse_parsed = true`, which is the weak-assertion failure this change is meant to fix.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_log_read_cache_config.py:111

chunk_findings.detail: The new `reuse_parsed = true` check is outside the existing false-direction loop and hard-codes `reporting.loops(repo)`. That means it does not exercise the true direction for any other real entry point in that loop. Concretely, if an unfixed call site other than `reporting.loops` hard-codes `LogConfig(reuse_parsed=False)`, the test still passes: the false-direction assertion for that site sees `_PARSE_CACHE` empty as expected, and the only true-direction call exercises a different call site. So the regression test does not actually fail on the intended bug.
